CogMap — self-repairing cognitive maps for robots

Phone walkthrough → world model → simulated swarm learns to navigate → the world changes → the swarm's failures repair the map → success recovers. Every map version is a W&B Weave evaluation.

Reflector post-mortem (gpt-5)

Round 1

Couch_2 was dragged into the chokepoint at (64, 46), creating a hard blockage the patrol did not preempt (0 changed cells). Evidence: success fell from 1.0 to 0.75 with 9 collisions and SPL dropped to 0.645625 (v1→v1-after-change-1). The swarm explored 40 cells, then executed 1 repair over 540 recovery steps using 3 rule ops and 1 LLM op (1 rejected). The fix restored zero collisions and success to 0.9375 (v3-repaired-1.1), updating the map to version 4.

Round 2

The armchair (goal for 4 tasks) moved to (50, 40). Patrol preempted the change (1 changed cell), but tasks still saw degraded performance: success 0.8125, SPL 0.7195625, and 3 collisions (v5-after-change-2). One repair over 875 steps with 9 rule ops (no LLM ops) resolved the mismatch, returning collisions to 0 and success to 0.9375 with minimal residual failures (v6-repaired-2.1); map advanced to version 7. Exploration added 40 cells.

Round 3

Couch_2 was put back, reopening the corridor, but the map still marked it blocked. Patrol preempted with 7 changed cells. Despite 1.0 success, SPL dipped to 0.71325 and collisions spiked to 4, indicating inefficient detours and map inconsistency (v9-after-change-3). Two repairs over 577 steps (5 rule ops, no LLM ops) cleared the stale obstacle, yielding 0 collisions and 1.0 success (v10/v11), with the map reaching version 12. Exploration added 25 cells.

What the swarm learned

Volatility centers on the busiest corridor chokepoint at (64, 46) and movable goal objects (armchair around (50, 40)). Even when patrol preempts, stale-map states can persist and degrade SPL and safety before repairs complete. Next, prioritize dense patrols and rapid validation sweeps around (64, 46) and (50, 40), add checks that specifically reconcile reopened paths, and trigger expedited repairs when collisions rise or SPL drops despite high success to clear false obstacles quickly.
